slot.brief: Find flux through one face of a cube/cubical arrangement with a charge placed at centre or corner or on a face; use symmetry division plus Gauss's law reasoning.

stem: A point charge $q$ is placed at one vertex of a cube. What is the electric flux through any one face of the cube that does not contain the charged vertex?

verdicts.working: The cube subtends one-eighth of the full solid angle at the vertex charge, so its total flux is q/(8ε₀). The three faces not containing the charge are symmetric, and the other three have zero flux; hence each of the three receives q/(24ε₀).

working:
Join eight identical cubes around the charged vertex; the charge is at the centre of the resulting cube.
$\Phi_{\text{large}}=q/\varepsilon_0$; hence the total flux through each small cube is $q/(8\varepsilon_0)$.
The three faces containing the charge have zero flux; the other three faces are equivalent.
$\Phi_{\text{face}}=q/(24\varepsilon_0)$

Independent check: The cube subtends one-eighth of the full solid angle at the vertex charge, so its total flux is q/(8ε₀). The three faces not containing the charge are symmetric, and the other three have zero flux; hence each of the three receives q/(24ε₀).
solution:
Join eight identical cubes around the charged vertex, placing the charge at the centre of the larger cube. By Gauss’s law, the flux through each small cube is $q/(8\varepsilon_0)$.
The three faces containing the charge have zero flux; symmetry divides the remaining flux equally among the other three faces:
$$\Phi_{\text{face}}=\frac{q}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{8\varepsilon_0}=\frac{q}{24\varepsilon_0}.$$
